flags.why: The ingredient restriction excludes bánh canh made entirely from rice flour, a common variety ([reference](https://www.banhcanhbotgao.com/tu-lam-banh-canh-bot-gao-ngon-chat-luong-tai-nha-cho-mua-dich.html)).
flags.fix: thick noodle soup (with noodles made from rice flour, tapioca flour, or a mixture)

flags.why: Bánh canh noodles can also be made entirely from rice flour ([reference](https://www.banhcanhbotgao.com/tu-lam-banh-canh-bot-gao-ngon-chat-luong-tai-nha-cho-mua-dich.html)).
flags.fix: thick noodle made from rice flour, tapioca flour, or a mixture

flags.why: Chống chế means to make excuses or offer a defensive explanation, not to fend off a physical condition ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/ch%E1%BB%91ng_ch%E1%BA%BF)).
Tụ hội has a literary register that the untagged entry conceals ([dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/tu-hoi-eQsRQEMp7xhvQ.html)).
The example confuses núc, meaning to entwine or squeeze tightly, with rúc, used for burying one's head against someone ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-n%C3%BAc)).
flags.fix: Con trăn núc chặt con mồi. = The python coils tightly around its prey.
